postTitle: Tax-Loss Harvesting and Asset Location Explained
topic: The same investments held in different accounts can owe less tax each year

assumptions.notes: Lesson example: €400,000 household, 70% shares, 25% bonds, 5% property companies. Same mix in every account: taxable account's bond interest and payouts cost €720 a year (30% rate). Placed by tax: the €720 goes; €60,000 more shares in the taxable account add about €180 of dividend tax (2% yield at 15%). Net about €540 less a year.

caption.instagram:
The same investments, held in different accounts. Could that change your yearly tax?

The example: a household with €400,000 across three accounts, 70% shares, 25% bonds and 5% property companies. With the same mix in every account, bond interest and payouts in the taxed account cost €720 a year at a 30% rate. Holding those in a tax sheltered account removes that. The shares that take their place add about €180 of dividend tax back. Net: about €540 less tax a year, and the overall mix has not changed.

The catches: each account becomes lopsided, keeping the mix on target takes more attention, and money in a sheltered account may be taxed when it comes out.
